answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via hardware attestation rooted in secure enclaves. Identities require cryptographic proofs generated by tamper-proof silicon keys. Instead of cloning bots across a network tundra, an attacker must incur verifiable capital costs purchasing physical processors for each execution thread, pushing mass forgery over a prohibitive cost ledge. However, the mechanism relies on centralized chip vendors and remains vulnerable to hardware side-channel leaks.
